title: Akron’s fan-turned-offensive coordinator learns in 4 plays football rarely goes to script
content:
Marty Whims II, an Akron alumnus and longtime season ticket holder, lived every fan’s dream when he moved from the seats to the sidelines Saturday afternoon and called plays for the Zips.

Whims was named Offensive Coordinator of the Game after he won a random drawing of season-ticket holders, which allowed him to design the opening drive of the game with Akron head coach Joe Moorhead.

It took some good fortune for Whims to land the opportunity. Unfortunately for Whims and Akron, that luck didn’t carry over to Saturday’s game against FCS foe Robert Morris. The Zips’ opening drive lasted just four plays and ended with a fumble just as Akron was about to pick up a first down and move deeper into Colonials’ territory.

Quarterback Cibastian Broughton dropped back on third-and-6 and hit receiver Marcel Williams, who was second-team All-MAC last season, for a short gain. But Williams fumbled the ball and Robert Morris recovered.

The Zips were in that third-and-6 situation only because they committed a false start penalty on third-and-1. Akron picked up 21 yards on the first three plays that Whims helped call.

Akron athletic director Andrew Goodrich hatched the idea on a flight after the men’s basketball team lost to Texas Tech in the first round of the NCAA Tournament this past March.

“We had this great fan interaction (in Tampa), and when I sat on the plane, I was like, ‘How in the world do we bring that kind of energy to a football game?’” Goodrich said in an interview with The Athletic this summer. “How do we do it? Honestly, it’s a long flight back, and we’re just racking our brains.”

Moorhead is in his fourth season on the job and went 5-7 last year, narrowly missing the program’s first bowl game since 2017.

The promotion was unveiled in August and led to nationwide attention; the post announcing the contest attracted more than 20 million views on X. Akron sold out its allotment of season-ticket suites and set a record for new season-ticket memberships.

Whims was named the contest winner on Aug. 25. He made an appearance Saturday on ESPN’s “College GameDay” and said he worked with Moorhead to create “a script of 20 plays that we can select from.”

Earlier in the segment, Nick Saban gave Whims three tips for his play-calling debut: 1. Get the call in early. 2. Stay ahead of the sticks — run the ball. 3. Don’t get cute, “but if you’re going to get cute, throw a damn flea flicker. Fans will love it,” Saban said.

But as the game proved, not much in football goes exactly to script.

Akron, however, on its next possession, used nine plays to drive 86 yards for a touchdown.
